content: When a medication is expired or no longer needed, it should be properly discarded. The information provided here was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that this document is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Depending on the specific product, this medication is administered either by injection into a vein or a muscle. It should be used exactly as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. If you are also taking aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin), administer them separately from this medication. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site. This medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. If used to treat syphilis or other spirochetal infections (e.g., Lyme disease), it may cause a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, which typically occurs 1 to 2 hours after administration and can last up to 24 hours. Rarely, this medication may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, penicillin, cephalosporin antibiotics, or any other substances. Some products may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., corn in products with dextrose) that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Penicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Certain formulations of this medication may contain sodium or potassium. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine glucose tests), potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., kidney function, complete blood count, potassium/sodium levels) to monitor your condition. Attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Adding plans allows you to compare the formulary status of this medication with other drugs in the same class. To view formulary information, create a list of plans, which can be saved and edited at any time. Individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current details.
